The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- A large dark brown/black lesion at the top margin
- Scattered small dark spots on the leaf blade
- Some yellowing at the lower right margin

The large irregular dark lesion without clear concentric rings, combined with scattered smaller spots, points toward Late Blight as top candidate. Let me view one reference image.

The Late Blight reference shows extensive papery dark-brown lesions covering most of the leaf. The test image differs — it has one large dark lesion at the leaf tip plus scattered small dark spots with some marginal yellowing. This pattern is less consistent with Late Blight.

Reassessing against the symptom descriptions:
- The large dark irregular lesion at the top with no clear concentric rings argues against **Early Blight**
- The scattered small dark spots with marginal yellowing and one dominant larger dark lesion is consistent with **Late Blight** (dark brown, papery lesions) — the pale yellowish border at the lower right matches the "pale green or gray border" descriptor
- **Bacterial Speck** would show pinpoint-sized specks with distinct yellow halos, which doesn't match the large top lesion

The test image's large dark irregular apical lesion with associated smaller spots and marginal yellowing is most consistent with Late Blight, even though the reference didn't show an identical pattern.
